primary_finding.interpretation: Within the frozen modeled finite population, recovery policy did not change the primary trusted-recovery success proportion. The contact-aware P3 guard did not improve the primary success endpoint relative to P1.

cryptographic_profile_finding.interpretation: In this finite contact-capacity model, larger standardized cryptographic-object bundles were consistently associated with no better and often worse trusted-recovery success. This is a modeled byte-budget/contact interaction, not a cryptographic execution-speed or spacecraft-performance result.

deadline_finding_for_P1_and_P3.interpretation: The frozen logical recovery horizon strongly conditions modeled recovery feasibility for P1 and P3.

contact_regime_finding_for_P1_and_P3.interpretation: Despite equal complete-cycle byte capacity by design, contact timing/geometry changes modeled recovery success; the clustered regime is lowest in the prespecified P1/P3 comparison.

policy_state_tradeoffs.P0_HARD_CUTOVER: Same primary success and transfer/contact burden as P1/P2, zero legacy exposure, but mean logical control unavailability 10537/864 slots.
policy_state_tradeoffs.P1_STAGED_CUTOVER: Same primary success with zero control unavailability and mean legacy exposure 10537/864 logical slots.
policy_state_tradeoffs.P2_HYBRID_OVERLAP: Same primary success and P1-like legacy exposure, plus mean dual-epoch overlap 2941/864 logical slots; no primary success benefit in the frozen model.
policy_state_tradeoffs.P3_CONTACT_AWARE_STAGED: Same primary success as P1, zero control unavailability, mean legacy exposure 5399/432 logical slots, mean contacts lower than P1 by 1/48, mean modeled cryptographic bytes lower by 124909/288, and mean transition attempts lower by 101/864.

failure_state_observation.boundary: These are aggregate terminal-state distributions. No post-hoc row-level failure-transition mapping is claimed under S8-SAP-001.

material_limitations: The policy factor is null on the primary success endpoint in this frozen model.
P3 changes modeled resource/failure-state behavior but does not create contact capacity and does not improve primary success.
P2 overlap changes policy-state exposure but yields no primary success advantage here.

The strong cryptographic-profile result is attributable to standardized object-size budgets interacting with the synthetic contact model and must not be presented as measured PQC algorithm performance.
The 3,456 observations are the complete deterministic modeled population, so no superpopulation sampling inference is supported.
